data.title: Alternative rapamycin treatment regimens mitigate the impact of rapamycin on glucose homeostasis and the immune system
data.authors: Arriola Apelo SI; Neuman JC; Baar EL; Syed FA; Cummings NE; Brar HK; Pumper CP; Kimple ME; Lamming DW

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Mice given rapamycin every day (2 mg/kg) developed glucose intolerance (the glucose curve was about 71% higher), raised fasting glucose and insulin, and their pancreatic islets released less insulin. The same dose given once every 5 days did not impair glucose tolerance or insulin tolerance, and fasting glucose and insulin stayed normal. Dosing every 3 days was already too frequent. Pyruvate tolerance, a liver measure, was still impaired, about half as much as with daily dosing. The drug is cleared within about a week (blood half-life roughly 15 hours), so mTORC1 was not blocked continuously. The immune effect got smaller but did not disappear (regulatory T cells fell about 25% versus about 60% on daily dosing), and testis weight still dropped by about 60% versus 75 to 80%. Everolimus and temsirolimus blocked mTORC1 as well as rapamycin but disturbed glucose tolerance less. Boundary: young male mice treated for 2 to 8 weeks, side effects only. No lifespan or benefit was measured, so this shows that harm can be reduced, not that the benefit is kept (see ARR2016 and BIT2016).
data.abstract_excerpt: Inhibition of the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling pathway by the FDA-approved drug rapamycin has been shown to promote lifespan and delay age-related diseases in model organisms including mice. Unfortunately, rapamycin has potentially serious side effects in humans, including glucose intolerance and immunosuppression, which may preclude the long-term prophylactic use of rapamycin as a therapy for age-related diseases.

extracted_findings.effect: Intermittent regimens and rapalogs inhibit mTORC1 while largely sparing glucose tolerance and immune function; no survival endpoint was measured
extracted_findings.dose: 2 mg/kg rapamycin administered daily (1x/day), weekly (1x/7 days), once every three days (1x/3 days), or once every five days (1x/5 days) to 9-week-old male C57BL/6J mice for 2-8 weeks.
extracted_findings.sample_size: 9-11 male C57BL/6J mice per treatment group for glucose tolerance tests; 3-6 mice per group for blood rapamycin concentration; 4-9 mice per group for insulin/HOMA2 measurements; 6 mice per treatment for islet analysis.
extracted_findings.effect_size: Daily rapamycin treatment significantly impaired glucose tolerance (20–116% increase in blood glucose, 71% increase in AUC), while weekly (1x/7 days) or 1x/5 days rapamycin treatment did not impair glucose tolerance. Rapamycin 1x/3 days significantly impaired glucose tolerance. Daily rapamycin inhibited both mTORC1 (S6 S240/244) and mTORC2 (AKT S473) signaling, while weekly rapamycin only inhibited mTORC1.
extracted_findings.limitations: No lifespan or healthspan endpoint. Side-effect endpoints only; benefit retention is inferred, not tested.
